Integer factorization (N=∏p​pvp​(N))

Words: 219 Articles: 3
Number theory OurBigBook.com
Finding the prime factorization of a positive integer. It is distinct from primality testing: deciding that an integer is composite does not itself supply its factors. For a semiprime, knowledge of a nontrivial square root of unity gives a factor through a greatest common divisor calculation.

Factor base

Words: 51
Integer factorization OurBigBook.com
A factor base is a finite set of small primes, often with the sign factor −1 included, over which selected integer residues are completely factored. A smooth number supported on this set gives an exponent vector. Linear dependence of such vectors modulo two produces a product that is a square, enabling congruence-of-squares integer factorization.

Odd part of a positive integer (n=2v2​(n)d)

Words: 78
Integer factorization OurBigBook.com
The odd part of a positive integer n is the unique odd positive integer d obtained by repeatedly dividing n by two. The process terminates because the positive integers decrease. If 2rd=2se with d,e odd, then r>s would make e even and s>r would make d even; hence r=s and d=e. Two positive integers have the same odd part exactly when their ratio is an integral power of two. The odd positive integers therefore give representatives for the resulting equivalence classes.

Congruence of squares (a2≡b2(modN))

Words: 50
Integer factorization OurBigBook.com
A congruence of squares is useful for integer factorization because N divides (a−b)(a+b). If a is not congruent to either b or −b modulo an odd semiprime, greatest common divisor computations with a−b and a+b recover proper factors. Smooth relations combined to make all prime exponents even produce such congruences in sieve-based factorization methods.

Erdős-Turán inequality

Words: 24
Number theory OurBigBook.com
The Erdős-Turán inequality bounds discrepancy of a finite sequence on the circle by a smoothing error and exponential sums of its low Fourier modes.

Fermat number (Fn​=22n+1)

Words: 120 Articles: 1
Number theory OurBigBook.com
A Fermat number is Fn​=22n+1 for n≥0. Distinct Fermat numbers are coprime integers. Their prime divisors are constrained by the multiplicative order of 2 modulo that prime; this remains useful whether or not the Fermat number itself is prime. The initial value F0​=3 must be distinguished when a statement restricts to positive indices.

Prime divisor of a Fermat number (ordp​(2)=2n+1)

Words: 71
Fermat number OurBigBook.com
If a prime number p divides the Fermat number Fn​, it is odd and 22n≡−1(modp). The multiplicative order of 2 divides 2n+1 but not 2n, so it is exactly 2n+1. Fermat's little theorem then gives 2n+1∣p−1. For n≥1, every prime divisor is 1 modulo 4. A prime need not divide any Fermat number merely because it is 1 modulo 4: order 12 excludes the prime 13 from the whole family.

Bernoulli number (Bn​)

Words: 156 Articles: 3
Number theory OurBigBook.com
The Bernoulli numbers in the convention B1​=−1/2 are defined by t/(et−1)=∑n≥0​Bn​tn/n!. The first values are 1,−1/2,1/6,0,−1/30. The function t/(et−1)+t/2 is even, so all odd-index values beyond B1​ vanish.

Hyperbolic cotangent generating function for Bernoulli numbers (cothz=z−1+∑j≥1​(2j)!22jB2j​​z2j−1)

Words: 64
Bernoulli number OurBigBook.com
The defining generating function of the Bernoulli numbers, with B1​=−1/2, gives this identity of formal Laurent series by cothz=1+2/(e2z−1). Therefore acoth(az)−cothz is regular and odd. Integrating it gives the even formal logarithm of sinh(az)/(asinhz). Its even derivatives of order k at zero are 2k(ak−1)Bk​/k, while the odd derivatives vanish. This computes the cyclotomic higher logarithmic derivatives of symmetric cyclotomic units without introducing a spurious linear term.

Euler evaluation of even zeta values (2ζ(2r)=−(2r)!B2r​(2πi)2r​)

Words: 30
Bernoulli number OurBigBook.com
Expand the cotangent partial-fraction expansion at zero to obtain πcot(πz)=z−1−2∑r≥1​ζ(2r)z2r−1. Substituting t=2πiz in the generating function of the Bernoulli numbers gives the same Laurent series as z−1+∑r≥1​B2r​(2πi)2rz2r−1/(2r)!. Equality of Laurent coefficients proves the formula.

Generalized Bernoulli number (Bk,χ​)

Words: 32
Bernoulli number OurBigBook.com
For a Dirichlet character χ of conductor f, define the generalized Bernoulli numbers by
∑a=1f​χ(a)efz−1zeaz​=∑k≥0​Bk,χ​k!zk​.
(1)
They express special values of Dirichlet L-functions at nonpositive integers and occur in the interpolation formula for Kubota-Leopoldt p-adic L-functions.

Normal number

Words: 104 Articles: 2
Number theory OurBigBook.com
A real number is normal in base K≥2 if every word of r digits occurs in its base-K expansion with limiting overlapping frequency K−r, for every r≥1.

Normality and equidistribution under integer multiplication

Words: 42
Normal number OurBigBook.com
A number x is a normal number in base K exactly when (TKn​x) is an equidistributed sequence. A word of length r corresponds to a half-open interval of length K−r; these intervals form arbitrarily fine grids, which approximate any interval from inside and outside.

Absolutely normal number

Words: 32
Normal number OurBigBook.com
An absolutely normal number is a normal number in every integer base K≥2. The Birkhoff ergodic theorem and ergodicity of integer multiplication on the circle, followed by a countable intersection of full-measure sets, show that almost every real number is absolutely normal.

Natural density (d(S))

Words: 71 Articles: 2
Number theory OurBigBook.com
For S⊆Z≥0​, its natural density, when it exists, is d(S)=limN→∞​∣S∩{0,…,N−1}∣/N.

Upper asymptotic density (d(A))

Words: 34
Natural density OurBigBook.com
For a subset A of the positive integers, its upper asymptotic density is d(A)=limsupN→∞​∣A∩{1,…,N}∣/N. Unlike natural density, it always exists. If natural density exists, the two agree. Positive upper asymptotic density suffices for the Szemerédi theorem.

Full-density sequence

Words: 24
Natural density OurBigBook.com
An increasing sequence of integers has full density when its range has natural density one. Convergence in density of a sequence means that, for each fixed tolerance, the exceptional indices have natural density zero.

Lagrange's four-square theorem

Words: 16
Number theory OurBigBook.com
The Lagrange four-square theorem says that every nonnegative integer is a sum of four integer squares.

Arithmetic function

Words: 2k Articles: 60
Number theory OurBigBook.com
An arithmetic function is a function whose domain is the positive integers, usually taking values in the complex numbers.

Radical of an integer (rad(n)=∏p∣n​p)

Words: 41
Arithmetic function OurBigBook.com
The radical of a positive integer is the product of its distinct prime factors, with rad(1)=1. It is the squarefree integer recording which primes occur, independently of their exponents. Equality of radicals is equivalent to mutual divisibility by sufficiently high positive powers.

Total number of prime factors (Ω(n))

Words: 40 Articles: 1
Arithmetic function OurBigBook.com
The completely additive arithmetic function Ω(n)=∑p​vp​(n) counts prime factors with multiplicity, whereas the prime omega function ω(n) counts distinct prime factors.

Excess prime-factor multiplicity (Ω(n)−ω(n))

Words: 28
Total number of prime factors OurBigBook.com
The nonnegative arithmetic function Ω(n)−ω(n) counts the repeated occurrences beyond the first of each prime factor. Its expectation under uniform sampling from [N] is bounded by ∑p​1/(p(p−1))≤1, independently of N.

Additive function (number theory)

Words: 77 Articles: 3
Arithmetic function OurBigBook.com
An arithmetic function f is additive when f(mn)=f(m)+f(n) for coprime integers m,n. Equivalently, f(n)=∑pk∥n​f(pk). This concerns multiplication of integers, and differs from an additive function on a vector space.

Mean of an additive arithmetic function (Af​(x))

Words: 18
Additive function (number theory) OurBigBook.com
For an additive arithmetic function, the model mean is Af​(x)=∑pk≤x​f(pk)(1−1/p)/pk. The exact uniform expectation differs by O(x−1∑pk≤x​∣f(pk)∣).

Strongly additive arithmetic function

Words: 17
Additive function (number theory) OurBigBook.com
A strongly additive arithmetic function satisfies f(pk)=f(p) for every prime p and k≥1, so f(n)=∑p∣n​f(p). The prime omega function is an example.

Completely additive arithmetic function

Words: 16
Additive function (number theory) OurBigBook.com
A completely additive arithmetic function satisfies f(mn)=f(m)+f(n) for all positive m,n, equivalently f(pk)=kf(p). The total number of prime factors is an example.

Multiplicative function

Words: 396 Articles: 12
Arithmetic function OurBigBook.com
An arithmetic function f is multiplicative when f(mn)=f(m)f(n) whenever m and n are coprime.

Multiplicativity of an arithmetic function

Words: 20
Multiplicative function OurBigBook.com
Multiplicativity means f(mn)=f(m)f(n) whenever m,n are coprime integers. It allows values of an arithmetic function to be assembled from its values on prime powers.

Completely multiplicative function

Words: 21
Multiplicative function OurBigBook.com
An arithmetic function f is completely multiplicative when f(mn)=f(m)f(n) for every pair of positive integers m,n, without a coprimality condition.

Divisor sum

Multiplicative function OurBigBook.com
The divisor sum of an arithmetic function f is
F(n)=∑d∣n​f(d).
(2)
If f is multiplicative, then F is multiplicative as well.
Sum-of-divisors function (σ1​(n))
Words: 17
Divisor sum OurBigBook.com
The sum-of-divisors function is
σ1​(n)=∑d∣n​d.
(3)
It is the divisor sum of the identity arithmetic function n↦n.

Pretentious distance (D(f,g;x))

Words: 303 Articles: 7
Multiplicative function OurBigBook.com
For multiplicative functions bounded by one, the pretentious distance up to x is defined by
D(f,g;x)2=∑p≤x​p1−ℜ(f(p)g(p)​)​.
(4)
It measures how similarly f and g behave on primes.
Large Fourier coefficient criterion for pretentiousness (∣ν(t)∣≤ClogXe−D(f,nit;X)2)
Words: 87
Pretentious distance OurBigBook.com
Let X≥3, and let f be a normalized multiplicative arithmetic function supported on squarefree integers, with ∣f(p)∣≤1. Form the finite measure ν=∑n​f(n)n−1−1/logXδlogn​ using Dirac measures. Under the transform convention ν(t)=∫e−itudν(u), its Euler product is ∏p​(1+f(p)p−1−1/logX−it). Expanding its logarithmic modulus, and replacing the damped prime weights by 1/p up to X with Mertens first theorem, gives the displayed absolute bound, uniformly in real t. Hence ∣ν(t)∣≥δlogX forces D(f,nit;X)2≤log(C/δ). The distance expression still defines a nonnegative pretentious score for prime values bounded by one; its actual metric interpretation uses unit-modulus values.
Pretentious distance between one and the Möbius function (D(1,μ;X)∼2loglogX​)
Words: 43
Pretentious distance OurBigBook.com
Because μ(p)=−1, the squared pretentious distance from one to the Möbius function is twice the reciprocal-prime sum. The Mertens second theorem therefore gives D(1,μ;X)2=2loglogX+2B1​+o(1). In particular the distance diverges, illustrating that a multiplicative function can be far from the constant function even though both have unit-modulus prime values.
Prime-restriction metric for pretentious distance (D(f,g;X)2=21​∑p≤X​∣f(p)−g(p)∣2/p)
Words: 59
Pretentious distance OurBigBook.com
For unit-modulus prime values, pretentious distance is the Euclidean metric on the finite vectors (f(p)/2p​)p≤X​. On whole arithmetic functions it is only a pseudometric: it sees neither values on prime powers nor primes above the cutoff. Even for every cutoff, the functions one and μ2 have distance zero but differ on nonsquarefree integers. The norm representation proves the triangle inequality and identifies exactly the quotient on which separation holds.

D(f1​f2​,g1​g2​;x)≤D(f1​,g1​;x)+D(f2​,g2​;x).

An Archimedean character on the positive integers is the completely multiplicative function n↦nit for a real parameter t.

Halász's theorem bounds the mean of a bounded multiplicative arithmetic function in terms of its least pretentious distance from an Archimedean character. A large mean can occur only when this distance is small.

Modular exponentiation evaluates a nonnegative integer power modulo m. Repdigit (Rn​=db−1bn−1​)

Words: 126
Integer OurBigBook.com
A repdigit is a positive integer whose base-b expansion repeats one nonzero digit d. For b≥2, 1≤d<b and n≥1, the finite geometric series gives Rn​=d(1+b+⋯+bn−1)=d(bn−1)/(b−1). For example, 5(10n−1)/9 has n decimal digits, all equal to five.
Every prime number not dividing b divides infinitely many such repdigits. If it divides d, every length works. Otherwise, if it does not divide b−1, the Fermat little theorem gives divisibility for lengths that are multiples of p−1, and division by b−1 is justified by its modular inverse. If p∣b−1, the sum is congruent to dn modulo p, so lengths divisible by p work instead. A prime dividing b but not d divides none, since Rn​≡d(modp). This distinction prevents invalid cancellation of the geometric-sum denominator.

Euclidean division (a=bq+r,0≤r<b)

Words: 53
Integer OurBigBook.com
For an integer a and positive integer b, Euclidean division writes a=bq+r with unique integer quotient q and remainder 0≤r<b. For a≥0, repeated quotient-and-remainder steps yield the digits of a base-p expansion when b=p. The uniqueness follows because the difference of two permitted remainders cannot be a nonzero multiple of b.

For a positive modulus m, integers a,b are congruent when their difference is divisible by m. This is an equivalence relation: zero is divisible by m, changing sign preserves divisibility, and adding two divisible differences proves transitivity. Addition and multiplication respect it, because (a+c)−(b+d)=(a−b)+(c−d) and ac−bd=c(a−b)+b(c−d). Its equivalence classes are the residue classes used in modular arithmetic.

There are infinitely many prime numbers. Indeed, for any finite list of prime numbers p1​,…,pk​, the integer N=p1​⋯pk​+1>1 has a prime factor, by the Fundamental theorem of arithmetic. comes from an integer change-of-variable matrix of determinant −1. It therefore preserves the set of integers represented and reduces the form to u2+v2.

Euclid lemma

Words: 14
Number theory OurBigBook.com
If a prime divides a product of integers, it divides at least one factor.

Prime valuation

Words: 15
Number theory OurBigBook.com
The prime valuation v_p(n) is the exponent of p in the prime factorization of n.

Euler totient function (φ(n))

Words: 418 Articles: 8
Number theory OurBigBook.com
Euler’s totient function counts residue classes modulo n that are coprime to n.

Sum of reduced residues (∑1≤j<n, (j,n)=1​j=nφ(n)/2(n>1))

Words: 56
Euler totient function OurBigBook.com
The map j↦n−j is a bijection of the integers between one and n−1 that are coprime to n. If their sum is S, this bijection gives S=nφ(n)−S, so S=nφ(n)/2. This works even at n=2, where the single residue is fixed. The same identity follows from the weighted inclusion-exclusion principle by excluding multiples of the prime factors of n.

Integers whose totient divides them (φ(n)∣n⟺n=1 or n=2c3d, c≥1, d≥0)

Words: 96
Euler totient function OurBigBook.com
If n>1 is odd, its Euler totient function is even and cannot divide n. Otherwise write n=2c∏j=1r​pjaj​​ with odd primes pj​ and c≥1. Comparing powers of two in φ(n)∣n gives ∑j​v2​(pj​−1)≤1. Thus there is at most one odd prime p, with v2​(p−1)=1. Since p−1 divides φ(n), it divides n, and is coprime to p; with only the prime factors 2,p available it must be a power of two. Hence p−1=2 and p=3. Conversely, for c≥1 the prime-power totient formula verifies divisibility for 2c3d, and n=1 is immediate.

Totient divisibility along divisors (d∣n⟹φ(d)∣φ(n))

Words: 46
Euler totient function OurBigBook.com
Write n=∏pap​ and d=∏pbp​, with 0≤bp​≤ap​. The prime-power formula for the Euler totient function gives an integer contribution to φ(n)/φ(d) from each prime: it is pap​−bp​ when bp​>0, and pap​−1(p−1) when bp​=0<ap​. Multiplying proves the divisibility assertion, including d=1 with φ(1)=1.

Rosser–Schoenfeld totient bound (φ(n)/n>1/[eγE​loglogn+2.50637/loglogn])

Words: 65
Euler totient function OurBigBook.com
For n≥3, this explicit lower bound on the Euler totient function implies φ(n)/n=Ω(1/loglogn) as n→∞. Here γE​ is the Euler--Mascheroni constant. The prime-product formula also gives φ(r)/r≥φ(N)/N whenever r∣N, making the bound useful for certified quantum period finding. The relevant statement is a lower bound: the claimed universal upper estimate φ(n)=O(n/loglogn) would fail at primes. Equations (3.41)–(3.42) of Theorem 15 provide the primary bound: denisevellachemla.eu/Rosser-Schoenfeld-1962.pdf .

Elementary totient-ratio lower bound (φ(r)/r≥1/(1+log2​r))

Words: 45
Euler totient function OurBigBook.com
List the k distinct prime divisors of r in increasing order. The jth is at least j+1, and k≤log2​r. The Euler totient function product formula gives φ(r)/r≥∏j=1k​j/(j+1)=1/(k+1). This elementary bound is sufficient to show inverse-polynomial success probability for coprime phase labels in quantum order finding.

Euler theorem

Words: 49
Euler totient function OurBigBook.com
If a is coprime to n, then a raised to the power phi(n) is congruent to one modulo n.
Multiplication by a unit a permutes the reduced residue classes modulo n. Multiplying all classes before and after this permutation and cancelling their unit product proves aϕ(n)≡1(modn).

Multiplicativity of the Euler totient function

Words: 13
Euler totient function OurBigBook.com
For coprime positive integers m and n, the Chinese remainder theorem gives phi(mn)=phi(m)phi(n).

Finite fibres of the Euler totient function

Words: 35
Euler totient function OurBigBook.com
For each positive integer k, only finitely many n satisfy φ(n)=k. Indeed, every prime p∣n has p−1∣k, and the exponent of p in n is bounded because pa−1∣k.

Number theory OurBigBook.com
The Jordan totient function counts ordered k-tuples modulo n that together with n have greatest common divisor one. The inclusion-exclusion principle gives
Jk​(n)=nk∏p∣n​(1−p−k).
(115)

For a prime p, every integer a satisfies a^p congruent to a modulo p.

Fermat factorization tests successive r≥⌈N​⌉ until r2−N=s2, then returns N=(r−s)(r+s).

A rational number is a quotient of two integers with nonzero denominator.

Farey sequence (FQ​)

Words: 61 Articles: 1
Rational number OurBigBook.com
The increasing list of reduced rational numbers in [0,1] with denominators at most its level Q, including zero and one.

Farey fraction

Words: 42
Farey sequence OurBigBook.com
A member of a Farey sequence. Two distinct level-Q fractions have ordinary distance at least Q−2. On the quotient circle identify zero and one before forming a set; the shorter wrapped distance of two remaining distinct fractions obeys the same bound.

Reduced fraction

Words: 39
Rational number OurBigBook.com
A reduced fraction a/b has coprime integers a,b and positive denominator b. Distinct reduced fractions with denominators at most Q differ by at least Q−2, since their difference has a nonzero integer numerator over a denominator at most Q2.

Density of the rational numbers

Words: 9
Rational number OurBigBook.com
Between any two distinct real numbers lies a rational number.

Repeating decimal

Words: 16
Rational number OurBigBook.com
A real number is rational exactly when its expansion in any integer base is eventually periodic.

Eventually periodic positional expansion of a rational number

Words: 40
Rational number OurBigBook.com
A positional expansion in an integer base represents a rational number exactly when its digit sequence is eventually periodic. Long division proves the forward implication because only finitely many remainders occur; summing a periodic tail as a geometric series proves the converse.

Modular multiplicative inverse (a−1(modn))

Words: 22
Number theory OurBigBook.com
A modular multiplicative inverse of a modulo n is a residue a−1 satisfying aa−1≡1(modn). It exists exactly when gcd(a,n)=1.

Number theory OurBigBook.com
The Carmichael function λ(n) is the exponent of (Z/nZ)×, equivalently the least positive m such that every unit a satisfies am≡1(modn).

Multiplicative order

Number theory OurBigBook.com
The multiplicative order of a unit a modulo N is the least positive r for which ar≡1(modN).

Decimal period from multiplicative order (ordq​(10))

Words: 48
Multiplicative order OurBigBook.com
For q>1 coprime to 10, long division of 1/q has remainders rn​≡10n(modq) in 1,…,q−1. Its digits satisfy 10rn−1​=qan​+rn​. A congruence 10m≡1(modq) therefore makes the remainders and digits periodic with period dividing m. The least period is the multiplicative order of 10 modulo q.

Cyclic decimal divisibility

Words: 49
Multiplicative order OurBigBook.com
For an L-digit decimal integer n, moving its leading digit to the end gives a cyclic rotation c1​(n) satisfying
c1​(n)≡10n(mod10L−1).
(116)
Thus, when a modulus d divides 10L−1, every rotation has the same divisibility by d as n, up to multiplication by a power of ten.

For a unit a modulo N, the function x↦axmodN is periodic on the integers.

Equality ax≡ay(modN) holds exactly when the multiplicative order divides x−y, so one period contains no repeated values.

The extended Euclidean algorithm also computes integers x,y satisfying ax+by=gcd(a,b). When a and b are coprime, either coefficient gives the corresponding modular multiplicative inverse.

Linear Diophantine equation

Words: 114 Articles: 2
Euclidean algorithm OurBigBook.com
A linear Diophantine equation in two variables has the form ax+by=c with integer coefficients and seeks integer solutions.

All solutions of a linear Diophantine equation ((x,y)=(x0​,y0​)+t(b/d,−a/d))

Words: 65
Linear Diophantine equation OurBigBook.com
If a,b are nonzero integers, d=gcd(a,b), and (x0​,y0​) is one solution of the linear Diophantine equation ax+by=c, then all solutions are
x=x0​+db​t,y=y0​−da​t,t∈Z.
(117)
Subtract two solutions and use the fact that a/d and b/d are coprime integers. The linear Diophantine equation solvability criterion says that a particular solution exists exactly when d divides c; the extended Euclidean algorithm constructs one. This parametrization separates existence from the complete family of answers.

Linear Diophantine equation solvability criterion

Words: 31
Linear Diophantine equation OurBigBook.com
The equation ax+by=c has an integer solution exactly when gcd(a,b) divides c. Bézout's identity proves sufficiency, while every integer linear combination of a,b is divisible by their greatest common divisor.

Sum of two squares theorem

Words: 86 Articles: 1
Number theory OurBigBook.com
A positive integer is a sum of two integer squares exactly when every prime factor congruent to 3 modulo 4 has even exponent in its prime factorization.

Congruence lattice proof of the prime sum of two squares (Λ={(a,b)∈Z2:b≡ua(modp)})

Words: 59
Sum of two squares theorem OurBigBook.com
If u2≡−1(modp), this lattice has basis (1,u),(0,p) and covolume p. The Minkowski convex body theorem applied to a disk of squared radius strictly between 4p/π and 2p gives a nonzero lattice vector with 0<a2+b2<2p. The congruence makes its squared length divisible by p, forcing a2+b2=p. The strict radius bounds avoid assuming the critical-volume form of Minkowski's theorem.
